newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly rice cash market summary -- USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly rice cash market summary -- USDA.

text.p: In the South, rice prices were steady to $0.50 cents lower. Long grain milled rice was selling mostly at $19.50 per cwt, Medium grain traded mostly at $18.00 to $19.00, second heads were steady at $14.00 to $15.00 and brewers remain in very tight supply with few quotes at $14.75 to $15.25. However, no confirmed sales were reported. Rice by-products were uneven, mostly steady to $5.00 higher.
In California, prices were steady to weak with medium grain selling mostly at $19.50. Rice bran was uneven, near steady.
California rice ship loadings at the Port of Sacramento for the week ending November 23, 1996: the Ziya-K loaded 21,000 tonnes of U.S. No. 1 bulk medium grain milled rice destined for Turkey.

Inspections of California rice for export: There were 463,176 cwt of U.S. medium grain milled rice inspected for the week ending November 23, 1996. The yearly total since October 1, 1996 is 766,446 cwt compared to 853,458 cwt a year ago.

The following prices were for domestic shipment -- offers, FOB mills, milled rice, dollars per cwt, bagged. (All milled rice grade 2 not to exceed 4 percent brokens, except California grade 1. All second heads grade 4 or better)
